newsitem.title: GERMANY: German row over Bosnia repatriation intensifies.
newsitem.headline: German row over Bosnia repatriation intensifies.

text.p: A row between Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and a number of German states over the repatriation of Bosnian refugees intensified on Wednesday as the states said Kinkel's planned visit to Sarajevo was just a publicity stunt.

Lower Saxony Interior Minister Gerhard Glogowski, who earlier this week along with other state interior ministers pulled out of Kinkel's trip to Bosnia set for Thursday, said he believed the visit would accomplish little.

"This event will take place under the eyes of 45 journalists and accompanied by a long list of members of parliament. I believe the opportunity for debate that we wanted is no longer there," Glogowski said on German radio.

He added that German state ministers had already been to Bosnia twice with Kinkel and that without the participation of German Interior Minister Manfred Kanther there was little that could be achieved by the trip.
A spokesman for Kinkel criticised the state ministers for denying themselves the opportunity to learn more about the situation in Bosnia and for "hiding behind" Kanther.
The German interior ministry confirmed separately that there had never been any plan for Kanther to go on the trip.
Kinkel has repeatedly berated Germany's 16 states for deciding last October to compel Bosnian refugees to go back home if they failed to return of their own accord.
Kinkel, whose visit to Sarajevo is aimed at coordinating repatriation plans, has urged them to come up with a plan to return the some 320,000 refugees in a humane way.

But Berlin Interior Minister Joerg Schoenbohm said it had already been established that a return of the refugees was possible and that the presence of up to 15,000 aid workers in Sarajevo alone would make a repatriation of thousands of Bosnians feasible.
"From this point of view I can completely understand my colleagues when they say: we shall learn nothing new from this trip," Schoenbohm said on radio.
